label: Alex O'Connor, Frank Turek thinks that Evil…: The problem of evil's premise that there is man-made…
locator: Alex O'Connor, "Frank Turek thinks that Evil proves God's existence" (Alex O'Connor, 2016-08-23), 02:06–03:36: why things like stealing rape and murder are moral wrong
interpretation: O'Connor sorts the evil invoked against an all-loving God into natural evil (earthquakes) and man-made evil (murder and rape). He treats the second as moral wrongness and answers that 'the morals of human activity are entirely subjective'. Read as: the critic's man-made-evil premise says of something that it is bad, in the moral sense his metaethics is about. This replaces an earlier bridge that read Aquinas' metaphysical malum (obj. 1) as a moral badness ascription; that would have equivocated between privation and moral language (Codex P1 on #160). Natural evil is not covered: O'Connor says we call it evil 'because they're harmful to us', a different claim. Wording from YouTube auto captions (caption_auto), not yet checked against the audio; 'moral wrong' is probably 'morally wrong'. Speaker: attributed to O'Connor by content, not mechanically confirmed.
